doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Horace Silver
summary: Johnson's first impression is Silver's rhythmic foot tap and swing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What about Horace Silver? Your first time playing with a guy who would be synonymous with that second generation of hard bop, of bop?
The first impression I had of Horace is a very strange one. I loved the tapping of his feet as much as his playing.

He has the most rhythmic foot tap of most musicians. [laughs] The whole ball and toe of his shoe would come up about six inches off the floor with every beat of the piece. He was a one-man rhythm section in that sense. Yet he could swing. We all know how hard Horace Silver could swing. He had an East Indian look about him. His hair would be falling down in his face and the perspiration would be falling down on the keyboard and swing, swing, swing, swing, swing. Beautiful. And a wonderful person, wonderful persona.
